title: The Ashwalker's Path
summary: Guide a desperate group across the Ashfields — a ruined heartland still burning twenty years after the Sundering — before your water runs out and the ash gets in.
world: Twenty years ago, the Sundering cracked the Ironplain and unleashed a magma column that burned for seven years. The resulting firestorm scorched the heartlands into the Ashfields: four hundred miles of grey cinders, sulfur vents, skeletal blackwood forests, and ash drifts deep enough to swallow a horse. The sky over the Ashfields is permanently orange-grey; the sun appears only as a pale smear. The surviving city-states cling to the margins: Crestwall in the north (military, fortified, trading hub), the Freeports on the western coast (merchant confederacy), and the Holdfast Cantons in the eastern mountains (isolationist, self-sufficient). Overland travel between them requires either a three-week coastal bypass or the Ashwalker's Path — a six-to-twelve day crossing of the Ashfields used by guides, smugglers, and the desperate. Ashwalkers are the people who know the Path's secrets: which sulfur vents erupt at what hour, where the ember worm nests are marked by white ash circles, where the Burnborn settlements are and whether they welcome visitors. The Burnborn are humans who survived prolonged ash exposure; they are changed — ashen skin, reduced need for water, amber-tinted eyes, heightened resilience — and they have built a society in the ruins. Some are hostile to outsiders, most are territorial, a few trade. Water is scarce: there are three known clean-water relay stations along the Path, spaced unevenly, and their condition varies. The Ashfields are beautiful in a dead, end-of-world way. They are also trying to kill you at all times.
openingScene: The last green tree is fifty yards behind you. The ash starts gently — a fine grey powder that coats your boots first, then your hands, then the inside of your throat. The sky closes down to a lid of orange-grey cloud. Three people follow you into the grey: Clem, a young cartographer who stops every twenty minutes to note something in her journal and seems genuinely delighted by all of this; Peris, a physician making for Crestwall with a satchel she has not once let out of arm's reach and will not discuss; and Wick, a retired soldier in his sixties who claims he has walked this route before, though he cannot remember exactly when or with whom. Your water supply — six full skins shared among four people — is good for four days if rationed. The Path, under good conditions, takes twelve. The first relay station is two days out. You have a compass, a hand-drawn map of uncertain accuracy, and the knowledge that ember worms are most active at dusk. You begin walking.
rulesNotes: Standard D&D 5e with survival mechanics layered on top. Ash lung: after each long rest in the Ashfields without ash protection, the player makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 12). First failure: disadvantage on further CON saves. Second failure: maximum HP reduced by 1d6. Third failure: unconscious and dying. Wet cloth over face (requiring a garment soaked in water from inventory) gives advantage on the save; it costs half a water skin's worth of water to wet. Water tracking: the group needs 1 gallon (one full skin) per person per day; the DM tracks this and narrates warning signs (dry lips, slower pace, headaches) as supplies run low. Encounters: Ember Worms (use Giant Centipede stat block at CR 1/4, but increase to 2d10 swarms at dusk; fire damage immunity); Burnborn patrols (use Bandit stat block but not automatically hostile — CHA checks determine reaction); ash storms (treat as heavily obscured terrain, 1d4 hours duration, everything stops); relay stations (each has a 40% chance of being operational, 30% stripped of supplies, 30% occupied by someone). NPC companions have their own needs and secrets — the DM may develop sub-tensions between Clem, Peris, and Wick as the journey lengthens. The campaign ends when the party reaches Crestwall or is destroyed trying. Recommended level: 4–7. Tone: gritty cinematic survival, dark wonder, slow dread.
